concepts.why: The patient presented with sudden vision loss and optic disc swelling, and imaging studies showed focal enhancement along the enlarged right optic nerve, with a hypercellular sample from the vitreous biopsy showing astrocytic neoplasm.

The patient developed sudden vision loss with no light perception, and examination showed marked swelling of the optic disc, peripapillary retinal hemorrhages, and occlusion of the superior branch artery.

The patient presented with sudden vision loss, and examination showed peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery, with combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein on follow-up.
The patient presented with blurred vision and optic disc swelling, with mild swelling of the optic disc on initial examination and marked swelling on follow-up.

The vitreous biopsy showed a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, with positive immunohistochemistry for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, and p53.

rationales.F01: Blurred vision in one eye could indicate optic nerve involvement, suggesting glioma of optic nerve.
rationales.F04: Relative afferent pupillary defect is a sign of optic nerve dysfunction, supporting glioma of optic nerve.
rationales.F05: Mild swelling of the optic disc is a common finding in optic disc edema, which could be caused by various conditions including glioma of optic nerve.
rationales.F06: No light perception vision indicates severe visual impairment, which could be caused by central retinal artery occlusion, retinal vein occlusion, or glioma of optic nerve.
rationales.F10: Focal enhancement along the enlarged optic nerve on MRI suggests optic nerve involvement, supporting glioma of optic nerve.
rationales.F11: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm on vitreous biopsy is diagnostic of astrocytic neoplasm, which is a type of glioma.
rationales.F12: Positive immunohistochemistry results for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, and p53 support the diagnosis of astrocytic neoplasm, a type of glioma.

frontier_selector.rationale: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm and positive immunohistochemistry results specifically support Astrocytic neoplasm, which explains the optic disc swelling and vision loss.
